Description: Verify a caller-supplied X-Request-Id is used verbatim and echoed in the response header (worked example 1)
Steps: Call GET /health with request header X-Request-Id: 'plrs59-<dynamic_id>'
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id equals 'plrs59-<dynamic_id>'. Response body is unchanged: {'status': 'ok', 'service': 'plrs'}

Description: Verify the server generates a uuid4 when the caller sends no X-Request-Id — downstream must always have a value (worked example 2)
Steps: Call GET /health with NO X-Request-Id request header
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id is present, non-empty, and is a valid version-4 UUID (36 characters)

Description: Verify two headerless requests get DIFFERENT ids — proving the id is per-request, not a shared global
Steps: Call GET /health with no X-Request-Id header; Call GET /health a second time with no X-Request-Id header
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK both times. The two X-Request-Id response header values are not equal

Description: Verify the caller's id is FORWARDED to the downstream stub — MockServer records a POST /charge carrying the same X-Request-Id (worked example 1, end to end)
PreRequisites: Execute SQL: INSERT INTO owners (id, name, email, subscription_active, subscription_fee) VALUES (<dynamic_id>, 'Corr Owner', 'corr_own_<dynamic_id>@plrs.test', true, 300); Execute SQL: INSERT INTO drivers (id, name, email) VALUES (<dynamic_id>, 'Corr Driver', 'corr_drv_<dynamic_id>@plrs.test'); Execute SQL: INSERT INTO lots (id, name, owner_id, hourly_rate, wall_code) VALUES (<dynamic_id>, 'Corr Lot', <dynamic_id>, 40, '1234'); Execute SQL: INSERT INTO spots (id, lot_id, code, is_active) VALUES (<dynamic_id>, <dynamic_id>, 'CR-1', true); Execute SQL: INSERT INTO reservations (id, driver_id, spot_id, lot_id, start_time, end_time, status, price, lock_expires_at) VALUES (<dynamic_id>, <dynamic_id>, <dynamic_id>, <dynamic_id>, NOW(), NOW() + INTERVAL '2 hours', 'SOFT_LOCKED', 80, NOW() + INTERVAL '5 minutes'); Mock POST /charge to return HTTP 200 with JSON {'status': 'SUCCESS', 'txn_id': 'mock_txn_888'}
Steps: Call POST /bookings/<dynamic_id>/confirm with request header X-Request-Id: 'plrs59-fwd-<dynamic_id>'
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id equals 'plrs59-fwd-<dynamic_id>'
Post-Assertions: MockServer has recorded exactly 1 POST /charge whose request header X-Request-Id equals 'plrs59-fwd-<dynamic_id>'
Teardown: Execute SQL: DELETE FROM payments WHERE reservation_id = <dynamic_id>; Execute SQL: DELETE FROM reservations WHERE id = <dynamic_id>; Execute SQL: DELETE FROM spots WHERE id = <dynamic_id>; Execute SQL: DELETE FROM lots WHERE id = <dynamic_id>; Execute SQL: DELETE FROM drivers WHERE id = <dynamic_id>; Execute SQL: DELETE FROM owners WHERE id = <dynamic_id>

Description: Verify an EMPTY X-Request-Id is replaced by a generated uuid4, not refused and not passed on empty (worked example 3)
Steps: Call GET /health with request header X-Request-Id set to an empty string
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK (never a 4xx — a tracing header cannot fail a request). Response header X-Request-Id is a valid version-4 UUID and is not empty

Description: Verify surrounding whitespace is stripped and the trimmed token is used (worked example 5)
Steps: Call GET /health with request header X-Request-Id: 'trim-<dynamic_id>   ' (three trailing spaces)
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id equals exactly 'trim-<dynamic_id>' with no surrounding whitespace

Description: Verify an id of exactly 128 characters is ACCEPTED — the limit is inclusive (worked example 6)
Steps: Call GET /health with request header X-Request-Id set to the character 'a' repeated exactly 128 times
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id equals the same 128-character value verbatim

Description: Verify an id of 129 characters — one over the limit — is replaced by a generated uuid4 (worked example 7)
Steps: Call GET /health with request header X-Request-Id set to the character 'a' repeated exactly 129 times
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id is a valid version-4 UUID (36 characters) and is NOT the 129-character value that was sent

Description: Verify an id containing a space is rejected as unusable and replaced — the header-injection guard, since a caller-supplied value is copied into an outbound header (worked example 8)
Steps: Call GET /health with request header X-Request-Id: 'has space'
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id is a valid version-4 UUID and is NOT 'has space'

Description: Verify an ERROR response also carries the header — a client that just saw a failure can quote the id that produced it
Steps: Call POST /bookings/<dynamic_id>/confirm for a reservation id that does not exist, with request header X-Request-Id: 'plrs59-err-<dynamic_id>'
ExpectedResult: HTTP 404 Not Found with JSON {'detail': 'Booking not found'} unchanged. Response header X-Request-Id equals 'plrs59-err-<dynamic_id>'

Description: Verify the web (PWA) layer is covered by the same middleware — it is registered before every router, not only the JSON API
Steps: Call GET /web with request header X-Request-Id: 'plrs59-web-<dynamic_id>'
ExpectedResult: HTTP 200 OK. Response header X-Request-Id equals 'plrs59-web-<dynamic_id>'
